message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-09-10 05:10 IST to 2026-09-11 05:10 IST (2026-09-09 23:40 UTC to 2026-09-10 23:40 UTC)

This primary product scan read, normalized, and deduplicated only `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt`. Ten credible, newly published Ubuntu security notices matched the monitored Ubuntu scope; two also directly match the separately listed Python and Microsoft .NET products. Product exposure depends on the Ubuntu release and whether the affected package is installed.

### Findings

**Finding 1 — Ubuntu Linux kernel for NVIDIA systems (USN-8748-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, `linux-nvidia-6.17`
- **Issue:** 27 Linux kernel CVEs, including CVE-2026-53215, CVE-2026-52955, and CVE-2026-53055
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** Canonical fixed flaws across hardware crypto, NVIDIA Tegra, network and file-system drivers, networking, Netfilter, Open vSwitch, and session-socket subsystems that could be used to compromise the system.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored; this applies specifically to Ubuntu 24.04 systems using the NVIDIA 6.17 kernel.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8748-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8748-1)

**Finding 2 — Ubuntu Beets package (CVE-2026-42052 / USN-8747-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 16.04 through 26.04 LTS, `beets`
- **Severity:** Not stated by Canonical
- **Description:** Malicious media metadata could inject HTML or JavaScript into the Beets web interface.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires Beets to be installed.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8747-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8747-1)

**Finding 3 — Ubuntu libEBML package (CVE-2023-52339 / USN-8746-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 16.04, 18.04, 20.04, and 22.04 LTS, `libebml`
- **Severity:** Not stated by Canonical
- **Description:** Specially crafted input could cause libEBML to crash.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires the affected library.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8746-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8746-1)

**Finding 4 — Ubuntu KissFFT package (CVE-2025-34297, CVE-2026-41445 / USN-8745-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS, `kissfft`
- **Severity:** Not stated by Canonical
- **Description:** Crafted transform sizes could crash KissFFT or permit arbitrary code execution, including an architecture-specific flaw on 32-bit systems.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires KissFFT to be installed.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8745-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8745-1)

**Finding 5 — Python on Ubuntu (USN-8744-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Python 2.7 and Python 3.4–3.14 packages across Ubuntu 14.04 through 26.04 LTS
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-3644, CVE-2026-4224, CVE-2026-4360, CVE-2026-6019, CVE-2026-15308
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** The fixes address cookie content injection, XML-parser recursion denial of service, tar hard-link filter bypass, JavaScript injection, and excessive CPU consumption in HTML parsing.
- **Relevance:** Both Ubuntu and Python are explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8744-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8744-1)

**Finding 6 — PHP on Ubuntu (USN-8743-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS, PHP packages
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-17544, CVE-2026-7260, CVE-2026-17543
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** Canonical published fixes for several PHP security issues.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires PHP to be installed.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8743-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8743-1)

**Finding 7 — GNU C Library on Ubuntu (USN-8737-2)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, `glibc`
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-77117, CVE-2026-19499, CVE-2026-6791, plus three additional CVEs listed by Canonical
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** The update carries Ubuntu 24.04 fixes for memory-safety and input-handling flaws, some of which could cause denial of service or arbitrary code execution.
- **Relevance:** glibc is a core Ubuntu component, so affected 24.04 systems are plausibly in scope.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8737-2](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8737-2)

**Finding 8 — Netty on Ubuntu (CVE-2026-47691 / USN-8742-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, `netty`
- **Severity:** Not stated by Canonical
- **Description:** A Netty flaw could expose applications to cache poisoning.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires Netty to be installed.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8742-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8742-1)

**Finding 9 — Flatpak on Ubuntu (CVE-2026-34078, CVE-2026-34079 / USN-8741-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu 18.04, 20.04, 22.04, and 24.04 LTS, `flatpak`
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** A malicious or compromised Flatpak app could use path-validation weaknesses to access host files, execute code in the host context, or delete arbitrary host files.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package notice; exposure requires Flatpak to be installed.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8741-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8741-1)

**Finding 10 — Microsoft .NET on Ubuntu (CVE-2026-58649, CVE-2026-69806 / USN-8740-1)**

- **Affected product/component:** .NET 8 and .NET 10 packages on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS
- **Severity:** Not stated at bulletin level
- **Description:** Cross-origin WebSocket validation in BrowserRefreshServer could expose information, while argument handling in AspireServerService could enable privilege elevation and arbitrary code execution.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu and Microsoft .NET are both explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8740-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8740-1)

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

A dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, and major officially maintained libraries and services. No credible MongoDB-related vulnerability was newly reported or materially updated inside this scan window.

MongoDB's authoritative alerts page shows its newest security batch dated September 8, 2026, before this run's cutoff, so those items were excluded as stale. [MongoDB Alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts)

### Possible matches needing review

None.

### Closing

Prompt review of the applicable Ubuntu systems is recommended, especially where the affected Flatpak, KissFFT, .NET, glibc, or NVIDIA-kernel packages are installed because Canonical describes possible host code execution or system compromise. No separately verified in-window disclosure was retained for the other monitored products.
